scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: Dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-02.statement: Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 are ESTIMATED read type and 1785 are ACTUAL read type.

F-04.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log contains 0 records, i.e. no tariff changes are logged.

F-05.statement: Field route completion for manual-read accounts (9200) was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for the 2026-08..09 period.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 states the utility may request route priority changes, which are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes query returned 14 routes with distinct completion values; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle shows 320 distinct accounts across 40 distinct routes were estimated in the latest billing cycle.

F-09.statement: mdms-export.read_events_for_disputed_estimated: 1184 AMI read events arrived before cutoff and were exported to billing but rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; 56 events had no AMI read received and were not exported.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-PROBLEM.statement: Dispute volume is high mainly because tickets are answered too slowly/inconsistently; an AI auto-answer agent would resolve the surge without needing to find an upstream billing defect.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules (logged in DA-RULES) around August introduced systematic bill errors that are driving the dispute surge.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter reads from the contracted field service (MeterWorks) are failing to arrive or validate correctly via H-FIELD-BILL, forcing more estimate substitution and incorrect bills.

H-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI interval reads from the Telemetrix MDMS are not reliably reaching billing via the nightly H-MDMS-BILL export, causing missing/stale reads and bad bills.

H-ESTIMATE-LOGIC-MISCALIBRATIO.statement: The estimate-substitution logic used when no accepted read is available (regardless of upstream read-collection cause) is itself producing inflated/incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: The dispute surge is caused by insufficient field reading staff/headcount, as attributed by the Field Operations Manager.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: A billing-side defect (e.g., tariff misapplication or import validation processing) affecting bills built on accepted ACTUAL reads is a larger driver of the dispute surge than estimate substitution.

H-IMPORT-REJECT-HIGH-CONSUMPTI.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI meter reads flagged as high consumption (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution for 1184 AMI-metered accounts behind disputed ESTIMATED bills, independent of field staffing or route completion (E-12).

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data on 2440 dispute tickets shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA, so ticket handling speed is not currently breaching SLA; this undercuts the premise that the surge is a response-speed problem rather than a bill-accuracy problem.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 are ESTIMATED-read bills and 1785 are ACTUAL-read bills, so a majority (59%) of disputes involve bills built on accepted actual meter reads, not substituted estimates. This means any explanation resting solely on upstream read-collection failure causing more estimate substitution (AMI delivery, field reads, estimate logic) can at most account for the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputes, leaving the larger ACTUAL-type share unexplained.

CRM data shows dispute volume was stable near baseline in June-July (610, 590) and roughly doubled starting August and holding into September (1180, 1260), confirming the magnitude and onset timing of the surge quantitatively, but it does not identify what is causing the wrong bills.

The tariff change log returned zero records, so no tariff changes were made that could explain erroneous ACTUAL-read bills; this narrows H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR to the import validation processing mechanism, since the tariff misapplication mechanism it also named has no supporting log entries.

Field route completion for manual-read accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over 2026-08..09, covering 9200 manual-read accounts, i.e. roughly 12 percentage points of routes were not completed during the dispute-surge period. This is a quantified shortfall in manual meter-read collection but does not by itself identify why routes went incomplete (staffing, routing design, or other field-side causes).

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; as a non-authoritative stakeholder statement it is a claim, not independent proof, but it agrees in direction with the authoritative E-04 tariff_change_log result (0 records) rather than contradicting it.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims a shortfall of three meter readers since July causes routes to run late, so affected customers receive estimated rather than actual bills. This is an unverified stakeholder explanation for the mechanism behind the manual-read shortfall already quantified in E-05, not independent proof of staffing as the cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract document (E-08) authoritatively confirms the field dispatch route-change authorization pathway: the utility may request route priority changes but they are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation, matching the existing K-DISPATCH constraint rather than introducing a new finding about dispute causation.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes lists 14 individual routes with distinct completion rates (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), giving route-level granularity under the aggregate manual-read shortfall already quantified in E-05 (0.88 vs 0.95 target). It does not contain reader-assignment, routing-design or equipment data, so it does not by itself distinguish staffing shortage from other field-side causes.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing-side estimate-substitution population for the latest cycle comprises 320 accounts spread across 40 distinct routes (E-10), a wider route footprint than the 14 routes flagged as lagging in E-09. This indicates estimate substitution is not confined to the subset of routes with a confirmed completion shortfall, complicating a clean link between the staffing-driven route lag and the full estimate population underlying A-ESTIMATE-DISPUTE-LINK.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which if confirmed would remove the vendor-provisioning blocker that previously left the mdms-export read query ACCESS_PENDING. This is an administrative/access claim, not evidence about AMI read delivery or bill-error causation itself.

Of AMI read events behind disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 reads arrived before cutoff and were exported to billing but were REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at import, forcing estimate substitution despite a usable actual read; only 56 cases show a true non-delivery (NO_READ_RECEIVED, not exported). This points to a billing-side import validation rule rejecting high-consumption AMI reads as a major, previously unidentified driver of ESTIMATED-type disputes, distinct from field staffing/route completion and distinct from an AMI delivery failure.

U-ACTUAL-BILL-ROOT-CAUSE.question: What specific billing-side mechanism (e.g., an import validation rule change) is producing errors in the 1785 ACTUAL-read-type disputed bills?
U-ACTUAL-BILL-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Without this, no confirmed billing-side fix exists for the majority of disputes; any solution scope touching DA-RULES/DA-BILL stays diagnostic-only.
U-ACTUAL-BILL-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Pull the billing-config import validation rule-change log (DA-RULES) and correlate rule-change dates with the August dispute onset (E-03) and the 1785 ACTUAL-type disputes (E-02).
U-ACTUAL-BILL-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Ship diagnostic-only scope (investigate_billing_import_rule_changes, investigate_actual_read_bill_errors); perform no bill corrections until the root cause is confirmed and any correction is routed to Billing Operations for manual execution per K-BILLWRITE.

U-STAFFING-VS-OTHER-FIELD-CAUS.question: Is the field reader staffing shortage (E-07, stakeholder claim) the actual cause of the route-completion shortfall, or are other factors (routing design, equipment) involved?
U-STAFFING-VS-OTHER-FIELD-CAUS.decision_impact: Determines whether a staffing-focused remediation or a routing/equipment-focused remediation is the correct fix for the estimate-substitution leg of the surge.
U-STAFFING-VS-OTHER-FIELD-CAUS.resolution_path: Cross-reference route-log completion records (DA-ROUTE) by route segment and reader assignment to see whether the shortfall pattern matches the 3-reader gap claimed in E-07 or correlates with other factors.
U-STAFFING-VS-OTHER-FIELD-CAUS.safe_placeholder: Treat H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE as unconfirmed; keep the route-completion work diagnostic only, with no field-dispatch change beyond the already-authorized, confirmation-gated push_route_update.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-ACCURACY-ME.question: Does a drop in dispute ticket volume reliably indicate improved bill accuracy, or could an auto-answer agent reduce visible tickets while wrong bills persist?
U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-ACCURACY-ME.decision_impact: If volume alone is used as the success signal, an auto-answer agent could mask ongoing billing defects instead of fixing them.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-ACCURACY-ME.resolution_path: Track M-ACTUAL-TYPE-DISPUTE-COUNT and M-ESTIMATE-BILL-SHARE alongside M-DISPUTE-VOLUME over the same post-remediation window to confirm volume decline coincides with reduced erroneous bills, not just suppressed ticket creation.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-ACCURACY-ME.safe_placeholder: Do not treat dispute-volume reduction alone as success; require the bill-accuracy metrics to improve concurrently before crediting ticket-template changes with resolving the surge.

U-HANDOFF-DATA-QUALITY.question: Are the H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL handoffs delivering complete, semantically valid read data to billing (both marked delivery_status/semantic_validity UNKNOWN)?
U-HANDOFF-DATA-QUALITY.decision_impact: Unverified handoff quality could itself be contributing to estimate substitution or ACTUAL-type bill errors, which would change where remediation effort should be targeted.
U-HANDOFF-DATA-QUALITY.resolution_path: Check H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL delivery and semantic-validity records against billing-side import logs; both are currently UNKNOWN in state.
U-HANDOFF-DATA-QUALITY.safe_placeholder: Treat both handoffs as unverified; do not rely on H-FIELD-BILL or H-MDMS-BILL data quality to support root-cause conclusions until validity is confirmed.
U-HANDOFF-DATA-QUALITY.resolution: For the H-MDMS-BILL leg specifically, delivery is largely functioning (1184 of 1240 disputed-ESTIMATED AMI reads arrived before cutoff and exported); the dominant problem is a downstream import rejection (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not handoff delivery failure, while only 56 cases show a true delivery gap (E-12).

A-STAFFING-CAUSE.statement: The manual-read route completion shortfall (E-05) is attributable to the field reader staffing shortage described by SH-FIELD (E-07), rather than other field-side factors like routing design or equipment.

A-ESTIMATE-DISPUTE-LINK.statement: The 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-02) originate from the same Aug-Sep manual-read account population whose route completion fell short (E-05); the two datasets are not directly joined in evidence.

A-ACTUAL-BILL-DEFECT-INTERNAL.statement: Errors in the ACTUAL-read-type disputed bills (E-02) originate from an internal billing-side defect such as an import validation rule change, rather than external factors like usage changes.
